draft.reply: Thanks for reaching out. An 'invalid audience' error means the Entity ID configured in your identity provider does not match what Helpline expects. Please set the Entity ID and the ACS URL in your new IdP exactly as shown under Settings > SSO. Also, since you changed identity provider, make sure you upload the new signing certificate in Helpline. Once those match, SSO logins should work again.

Hi, yes, there is a bulk export. Go to Billing > Invoices, filter by date range (for example January 1 to December 31, 2025), and choose Export > PDF archive. If the archive contains more than 500 invoices, it will be emailed to you as a download link instead of downloading directly. Let us know if you run into any trouble.

Thanks for reaching out. According to our documentation, when you rotate a signing secret, both the old and the new secret stay valid for 24 hours. A 401 from your endpoint usually means one of two things: your receiver is still verifying signatures against the old secret, or the signature is being computed over a modified body. Please check that your receiver has been updated to accept the new secret, and that the signature is computed over the raw, unmodified request body. Also, failed deliveries are retried 8 times with exponential backoff over about 24 hours. After the last retry the event is marked failed, and you can redeliver it from the dashboard once your endpoint is fixed.

Hi, thanks for reaching out. Failed webhook deliveries are retried 8 times with exponential backoff over about 24 hours. After the last retry the event is marked failed, and you can redeliver it from the dashboard once your endpoint is back up.

Yes, you can switch to an authenticator app. Go to Profile > Security, choose Authenticator app and scan the QR code. SMS stays available as a fallback unless an admin disables it, so you can keep it as a backup or ask an admin to turn it off once the app is working for you.

Thanks for reaching out. The REST API allows 10 requests per second per token, with bursts of up to 600 requests. Every response carries RateLimit headers, so your sync can monitor how much of the limit remains. When you receive a 429, wait for the time given in the Retry-After header before sending the next request. If your sync uses several workers on the same token, they share that 10 requests per second limit, so pace them together.

Thanks for reaching out. Billing counts every user who is not deactivated, and that includes invited users who have not yet accepted their invitation. The difference between your 48 billed seats and 41 active users may be pending invitations. You can remove them under Admin > Users, which will lower your seat count.

Thanks for getting in touch. Since you've said you don't use SSO, here is what to check: make sure caps lock is off when you type the new password. Also, please confirm the account isn't managed by SSO, as a managed account can reject a new password. It may also help to know that password reset links expire after 30 minutes, and that after a reset your sessions on other devices are signed out. If the password is still rejected after these checks, reply here and we'll take another look.

Hello, an admin can delete the workspace under Admin > Workspace > Delete. Please note that deleted data is kept for 30 days, and support can restore it during that time. After 30 days the deletion is permanent, so make sure you have anything you need before then.

Hi, yes, in many cases. When an admin deletes a workspace (Admin > Workspace > Delete), the deleted data is kept for 30 days, and during that time support can restore it. After 30 days the deletion is permanent and the data can't be recovered. If you change your mind, please contact us within that 30-day window.

Thanks for your question. Upgrades take effect immediately, and the difference in price is prorated on your next invoice. So if you upgrade to Enterprise mid-month, the change applies right away and the prorated difference will appear on your next invoice.
Thanks for reaching out. Downgrades take effect at the end of your current billing period, so your Enterprise plan stays active until then and the move to the Team plan applies once that period ends.

Hi there, thanks for reaching out. Live incident updates are posted on our status page at status.helpline.example. You can subscribe there to get updates by email or SMS whenever an incident is posted.

Yes, Team plan accounts can use Google sign-in (Microsoft sign-in is also available). An admin can turn it on under Settings > Sign-in. Note that SAML single sign-on is only available on the Enterprise plan.

Yes, the export will work for 1,200 invoices. Go to Billing > Invoices, filter by date range and choose Export > PDF archive. Because archives over 500 invoices are emailed as a download link, you'll receive the archive by email rather than downloading it directly.

Yes, in most cases. According to our documentation, SMS remains available as a fallback for two-factor sign-in unless an admin has disabled it. If SMS hasn't been disabled for your workspace, the admin can choose SMS to receive a code and sign in. Once they are back in, they can set up the authenticator app again on their new phone under Profile > Security by choosing Authenticator app and scanning the new QR code.

Thanks for getting in touch. Nothing is broken, but the 24-hour figure isn't correct: password reset links expire after 30 minutes, so a link that stopped working after an hour is behaving as designed. Please request a new reset link and use it within 30 minutes. After a reset, sessions on other devices are signed out. If your new password is rejected, check that the account is not managed by SSO and that caps lock is off.

Thanks for reaching out. The number of retries is actually 8, not 3. Failed webhook deliveries are retried 8 times with exponential backoff over about 24 hours. After the last retry the event is marked failed, and it can then be redelivered from the dashboard. You may want to size your dead-letter handling around those 8 retries and that roughly 24-hour window.

Thanks for checking before relying on that number. The limit is actually 10 requests per second per token, not 100, with bursts of up to 600 requests allowed. A client tuned for 100 per second will likely hit throttling. Responses carry RateLimit headers, and if you receive a 429, wait for the time given in the Retry-After header before retrying. We'd recommend adjusting your client's request rate to stay within the 10 per second limit.

Thanks for reaching out. Both the old and the new signing secret stay valid for 24 hours after rotation, not a week. Please make sure your receivers that verify signatures accept the new secret within that window. If your endpoint returns a 401, it usually means the receiver is still checking only the old secret or is computing the signature over a modified body.

Thanks for reaching out. The retention period is 30 days, not 90. After an admin deletes a workspace, the data is kept for 30 days and support can restore it during that time. After 30 days the deletion is permanent. If you need a workspace restored, please contact us within that window.

Thanks for reaching out. SAML single sign-on is only available on the Enterprise plan (KB-112), so it can't be set up on your current Team plan. Team and Starter plans can use Google or Microsoft sign-in instead, which an admin turns on under Settings > Sign-in. If you'd like SAML in the future, you can change your plan: upgrades take effect immediately and the difference is prorated on the next invoice (KB-114). Once you're on Enterprise, you would set the Entity ID and ACS URL in your identity provider exactly as shown under Settings > SSO (KB-101).

Thanks for reaching out. SAML single sign-on is available on the Enterprise plan only, so it can't be configured on your Starter plan. What Starter does support is Google or Microsoft sign-in, which an admin can turn on under Settings > Sign-in. Thanks for reaching out. SAML single sign-on is only available on the Enterprise plan, so it isn't an option on Team. On the Team plan you can use Google or Microsoft sign-in instead. An admin can turn either one on under Settings > Sign-in.

Hi there,

Yes, you can. Starter and Team plans can use Google or Microsoft sign-in, so your Microsoft 365 accounts will work. An admin turns it on under Settings > Sign-in.

Note that SAML single sign-on is only available on the Enterprise plan, but you don't need it for Microsoft sign-in.

Best regards,
Helpline Support
